narrative.overview: felroz is Felipe introducing himself: the site is his calling card (la carta de presentación), for the day he looks for a job or for anyone who wants to know who he is. It opens like a conference badge with his face, a greeting and his name, then square cards on a dark table, each stating one fact about him in a single look with a small drawing in place of a paragraph. It closes with an invitation to talk. The warm gradient marks only the one thing that matters most; the dots answer the visitor's pointer and nothing moves on its own. Developer first; AI is one skill, never the hero.
keyCharacteristics: A badge first: face, greeting and name before anything else.
Square cards, one fact each, illustrated rather than written.
Dark Carbone ground, white text, warm gradient used as a single signal.
Symbol: a gradient f followed by a hollow node and a Pêche arrival dot.
Motifs: a pointer-reactive dot field plus dotted routes linking nodes, in the background or as single-colour card illustrations.
Cards with soft shadows and an offset hover that reveals a colored dot-grid layer.
DM Sans for everything human; DM Mono in spaced uppercase for everything machine.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: The gradient (left → right: Prune, Corail, Pêche) appears once per screen's content: one keyword or one accent. The persistent chrome (the symbol and the header's Contact button) does not count, as in the DA's own header. If two things in the page content are gradient, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Plain Text Rule
rules.body: Running text is white on Carbone or Carbone on Craie. Never gradient, never Corail.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: DM Sans and DM Mono only. No display or decorative faces.

rules.name: The Machine Voice Rule
rules.body: DM Mono is always uppercase with 2px tracking, and only for labels, code and metadata. Never for sentences, never as an eyebrow.

rules.name: The Split Card Rule
rules.body: Linked cards keep the offset hover: face translate(8px, -8px), underlayer translate(-8px, 8px), both with transition-all. Do not flatten it.

rules.name: The Motion Budget
rules.body: Two protagonists on load: the dot field and the hero greeting (once). Everything else moves only on interaction. Card entrance is one short CSS stagger; under reduced motion nothing animates.

dos: Do keep the gradient to one signal per screen (the One Signal Rule).
Do set running text white on Carbone, or Carbone on Craie.
Do use DM Mono, uppercase with 2px tracking, for labels, metadata and code.
Do keep the card shadow and the split offset hover on every linked card.
Do use the symbol from 24px up and the lone Corail f below 24px.
Do size UI to the longer French copy.
Do let headings stand alone: no eyebrow label above them.
Do keep home tiles square or whole-square, and keep the poster as the 3D avatar's fallback.
donts: Don't make an animation run at rest on the home (besides the dot field's pointer response and the greeting, once).
Don't draw the f with a crossbar. The decided mark has none.
Don't use the retired falroz wordmark or name.
Don't place routes or dotted lines behind text, or use dashed lines anywhere outside the route motif.
Don't add a second type family (Aclonica is retired).
Don't set body copy, paragraphs or long labels in gradient.
Don't use the third-party brand colors outside their own icons.
Don't replace the 3D card treatment with flat cards.
Don't make AI the hero: no agent diagrams, no fake logs, no "AI Engineer" as the loudest element.
Don't pitch: no "let's work together" sales copy, no invented metrics or placeholder text in production.
